issues.evidence: Sanskrit title is Ārya Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Nāma Mahāyāna Sūtra (Noble Perfection of Wisdom called the Diamond Cutter, a Mahāyāna sūtra); children's text gives only the short name (locked term maps the whole title to Diamond Cutter).
issues.fix: In the language of India: the noble perfect wisdom called the Diamond Cutter, a Great Vehicle sacred text.

issues.span: He finished eating his alms food.
issues.evidence: Academic: 'Having given up the alms of the later meal' - he set aside any further meal; children's text only says he finished eating.
issues.fix: He did not take any more food. He put away his alms bowl and teaching robe.

issues.span: with careful attention, ready to pay full attention
issues.evidence: Tibetan/academic: 'having established mindfulness to the fore' (one phrase, locked 'pay full attention'); the text splits it into two and adds 'ready to'.
issues.fix: He sat up straight and paid full attention.

issues.span: However many exist in the realm of living beings
issues.evidence: Academic: 'however many are designated by conceptual designation as sentient beings in the realm of sentient beings' - they are merely called/designated living beings; 'exist' asserts real existence and drops the designation point that sets up the paradox in 4-2.
issues.fix: However many are called living beings in the realm of living beings, I will lead them all to complete freedom from sorrow in the expanse of freedom from sorrow with no group left over.

issues.span: I must help all kinds of living beings.
issues.evidence: Academic has the thought 'all those I shall lead to complete nirvana'; 'I must help' adds an obligation and a different action (help vs lead to freedom from sorrow).
issues.fix: I will lead all living beings to freedom from sorrow. This includes...
